signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + BoJ Hawkishness
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.66, testing the SMA20 at 159.12 as risk-off flows intensify following reports of an Iranian attack on a Saudi vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. While the 270bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry advantage traditionally supports the pair, the BoJ chief's confirmation that rate hikes are 'on the table' for this month's meeting introduces a hawkish policy floor. Options markets show a clear bias for JPY strength, with the USD/JPY 25d Risk Reversal at -1.79 (strong put skew), signaling institutional demand for downside protection against potential intervention or carry unwinds. Despite the VIX at 16.5, the yen's correlation with the VIX has turned positive (+0.382 vs -0.159 norm), suggesting the JPY is currently trading more on policy repricing and geopolitical shock than broad safe-haven beta. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; hawkish BoJ pivot and Middle East escalation threaten the 160.00 ceiling. Catalyst: US ADP Employment data at 12:15 UTC. Risk: De-escalation in the Strait of Hormuz restores carry-first dominance.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Sell-the-Fact
signals.text: NZD/USD has plunged to 0.5824, breaking below its SMA200 (0.5853) following a 'sell-the-fact' reaction to the RBNZ interest rate hike. While the RBNZ raised rates to 2.75%, the market has characterized the move as part of a 'gradual path' that fails to support the Kiwi against a surging US Dollar. The USD 1W average performance sits at +0.923%, while the NZD has lagged G10 peers by -1.680%, creating a massive 2.603% leader-to-laggard spread. COT positioning for NZD is at a 52-week extreme (pctl 0, z -2.60), yet the failure of the rate hike to trigger a short-squeeze highlights the dominance of the USD's bear-flattener yield curve regime. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; gradual RBNZ path offers no relief against USD outperformance. Catalyst: US ADP Employment data today. Risk: USD bear-flattener reverses on a significant ADP miss.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3483, holding just above its SMA50/200 cluster (1.3436/1.3443) as the pair faces pressure from a crowded speculative long. CFTC data shows GBP leveraged funds are net long +56,839 (pctl 96, z +1.58), marking a significant positioning extreme that leaves the pound vulnerable to unwinding on data misses. Options markets are pricing in substantial uncertainty, with GBP/USD Implied Volatility (IV) at 11.0% against a Realized Volatility (HV30) of 5.0%, resulting in a massive +6.0% Vol Risk Premium (VRP). This elevated premium suggests that while price action has been relatively stable, the cost of hedging downside risk is at an extreme. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; crowded long positioning meets an expensive vol floor. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced). Risk: US 10Y yields retreat, allowing the neutral 0bp GBP/USD carry to attract dip-buyers.

signals.title: AUD/JPY — Carry vs Retail Extreme Divergence
signals.text: AUD/JPY is trading at 114.007, supported by a significant +335bp nominal carry advantage (RBA 4.35% vs BoJ 1.0%) despite recent yen strength. Retail sentiment via Myfxbook shows an extreme 86% short position, which traditionally serves as a contrarian indicator for upside continuation. However, this retail short-bias is currently aligned with institutional flows (JPY COT pctl 9) and the BoJ's hawkish policy shift, creating a rare institutional-retail alignment rather than a divergence. AUD's own real rate remains mildly accommodative at -0.55%, contrasting with the JPY's deeply accommodative -1.70%. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/JPY; retail extreme short is neutralized by BoJ policy hawkishness and geopolitical risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Sharp risk-on recovery in equities forces a retail short-squeeze higher.
